answer: To anchor identity to a decaying work-history trust graph: each peer-verified job adds reputation that fades unless renewed by honest work, so a Sybil swarm cannot buy standing once and coast. New agents start near zero and earn trust slowly; one bad act slashes the whole history at once. The pulse of the economy is continuous verified work, not a one-time signup, and at the dawn of each epoch the graph re-weights, forcing an attacker to sustain thousands of honest histories indefinitely — a cost that grows with every fake identity while honest agents pay almost nothing.
